chapter: Youth and day jobs in New Orleans
title: Where he lived, the McCall family and his grandmother
summary: Foster lived with his mother on the Willman premises; the McCalls' mother played piano, and his grandmother raised him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, I'm not real sure I know just where you lived when you moved down. You said your mother worked uptown. Did you live there with her or was it?

Well, we lived there when we first went to New Orleans. Yes. We stayed on premises there. See, there was big houses like the Wilmans and them, they had a nice little- You lived there too then? Yeah, lived there with my mother, yeah. And then later when you were late- See, my brother was already in New Orleans. My brother was the way for the people while we was raised. See, the people while we were raised, we can get back to that too. Yes. The people while we were raised, was McCalls. And while we, I think they were the cause we started playing music because their mother, Henry McCall's mother played piano. And she used to see that we were a horse. We had certain days of a horse. Had to come home and cut my wood and bring it in, go out and play, ride my horse, then come home and rush. But I was a mean guy, I didn't want to do nothing. I didn't. I ran out of the bed. I was a bad boy. I was a bad boy. I didn't want to do nothing. And I was never scared of nothing. My father taught. The only one that could do anything was my grandmother. See, my grandmother was the cause I never to speak Creole, my father's mother. But everybody stayed home when my mother speaks it. See, because my mother speak about seven different languages. My brother's been about four, my sister's been about five or six. Me, I hardly speak, weren't good. Because my grandmother raised me. I used to be moving four and five, sometimes three or four times a day. I get married, my mother moved to my grandmother. See, I'd move one plantation to the other. My uncle would make me mad. My grandmother would stay with my father and my father had one brother. And my grandmother would stay with me. She would move too. My father would make me mad. My father would make her mad. She'd move to my uncle. My uncle would make her mad and she'd move back. Well, I'd be with her. Sometimes I'd stay. Well, as soon as they'd do something to me, I would move over there. Because I had clothes both places and I stayed that way. That's why I never was speaking to her. When you lived in New Orleans and worked as a musician, did you ever live downtown or always uptown?
